newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-COACHES BIANCHI, PEREZ AND GALEONE ALL UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COACHES BIANCHI, PEREZ AND GALEONE ALL UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: Carlos Bianchi of Roma, Gregorio Perez of Cagliari, and Giovanni Galeone of Perugia are the latest in a long line of Serie A coaches to find themselves in the hot seat this week.
On Monday speculation suggested that Perez, the Uruguayan coach at Cagliari, was likely to be dismissed following his side's 2-1 away defeat by Lazio on Sunday.
Former AS Roma, Ascoli and Cagliari coach Carlo Mazzone is widely tipped to take over.

Cagliari President Massimo Cellino was reportedly disappointed by his side's inability to make more of its numercial advantage, after Lazio goalkeeper Luca Marchegiani was sent off after only four minutes. Cagliari are currently third from bottom with four points.
Bianchi of Roma was another Latin American coach to feel the heat after his team were beaten 2-1 at bottom club Verona.
Ten days ago, Roma sprang one of the surprises of the season when they beat champions AC Milan 3-0.

For Roma fans who had waited more than a decade for a league win against Milan and who last celebrated an Italian title victory 13 years ago, it seemed that the good times were just around the corner.
But Sunday's defeat plus a 3-0 loss at Karlsruhe in a UEFA Cup tie in Germany last week may have dampened such enthusiasm.
Already eliminated from the Italian Cup and with a difficult task ahead of them in the second leg of their UEFA tie, Roma are sudddenly in trouble.
Bianchi has come in for much media and fan criticism for the manner in which he has changed his side, in particular for leaving out strikers Francesco Totti and Argentine Abel against Karlsruhe.
Fans have also been critical of Roma's Argentine defender, Roberto Trotta, a player whom Bianchi insisted on importing from Velez Sarsfeld.
In Verona on Sunday, some Roma fans displayed a banner reading, "Go Away Trotta".
Galeone of newly promoted Perugia, is also under pressure this week even though his side keeps on winning.
Galeone and the Perugia owner, Luciano Gaucci have been at daggers drawn since a blazing row during a pre-season friendly tournament in Spain.
The tension seemed to be getting to Galeone last week when he went into hospital with suspected heart problems.
Out of hospital on Sunday and under doctors' orders to give up smoking, Galeone saw his side win 2-1 at Parma.
Perugia now have nine points, just four less than league leaders Juventus.
But even that good standing does not appear to entirely convince owner Gaucci.
"I got cross before when we didn't pick up the points we ought to have but now I don't see any reason to be angry or bring in re-inforcements.
"However, let's not fool ourselves, I'waiting to see how we go against Udinese in our next match".
